text: Dass. Let AB, ED, (fig. 8) be the incident rays tending to F, a point beyond the centre C, and let DR be the refleted ray of the incident one ED. Then because the incident ray ED tend to a point beyond the centre, the refleted ray DR will proceed as from one on the contrary to, flopode 2 as as- related above under Drop, VII. Through D draw the perpendicular CD, and produce it to H. Thus will EDH and HDD be the angles of incidence and re- flelections, while being equal, their vertical ones of DF and CDR will be fo to cases confiantly the vertex of the triangle FDR and bifled by the line CD+ where- fore, RD is to DF, or (3 Elem d o) BD vanthing, RB is to DF as RC to CF; that is, the dilatance of the focus of the refleted rays is to that of the imaginary focus of the incident rays, as the dilatance the lower from the center is to the dilatance of the latter from the fame. _@E.D._
